สังเกตขณะเยี่ยมติดตามผู้ป่วยที่บ้านร่วมกับโรงพยาบาลส่งเสริมสุขภาพตำบล และ อาสาสมัครสาธารณสุข ประจำหมู่บ้าน จากการสัมภาษณ์เชิงลึก พบว่า ตลอด 2 เดือนที่มีการติดตามผู้ป่วยเจ้าหน้าที่ของโรงพยาบาล ส่งเสริมสุขภาพตำบล โดยมีการกำกับการกินยาโดยมีการวิดีโอคอลตามเวลานัดหมาย จากนั้นนำมาบันทึกการ กินยาในโปรแกรม NTIP อย่างครบถ้วนถูกต้อง นอกจากนี้ในทุกๆ การนัดหมายการกินยาจะมีการนับเม็ดยาที่ เหลือควบคู่ไปด้วย จากการติดตามผู้ป่วยกินยาครบทุกวันทั้ง 32 คน ได้ไปพบแพทย์ตามนัดทุกคน นอกจากนี้ ในการปฏิบัติตัวและพฤติกรรมการดูแลสุขภาพปฏิบัติในด้านการกินยาและการป้องกันการแพร่กระจายเชื้อได้ อย่างถูกต้องมากขึ้น เนื่องจากได้รับคำแนะนำที่ถูกต้องจากเจ้าหน้าที่โรงพยาบาลส่งเสริมสุขภาพตำบล และได้ แนะนำผู้สัมผัสร่วมบ้าน จำนวน 50 คน ไปเอกเรย์ปอดที่โรงพยาบาลตามสิทธิ์การรักษาทุกราย พบผลปกติทุก ราย อีกทั้งผู้ป่วยมีการป้องกันการแพร่กระจายเชื้อได้อย่างถูกต้อง นอกจากนี้มีการสะท้อนผลของการปฏิบัติ ตามแผน สามารถแก้ไขปัญหาของผู้ป่วยวัณโรคปอดในพื้นที่จังหวัดนนทบุรีทำให้ผู้ป่วยได้รับการดูแลและกินยา อย่างต่อเนื่อง มีการปรับปรุงสิ่งแวดล้อมในบ้านเพื่อลดการแพร่กระจายเชื้อ รวมถึงมีการส่งต่อข้อมูลผู้ป่วยที่ เป็นความลับและสามารถส่งต่อได้อย่างถูกต้องรวดเร็ว ทั้งนี้ในการประชุมได้ทำการสรุปให้มีการติดตามผู้ป่วย อย่างต่อเนื่องทั้งการกำกับการกินยาผ่านวิดีโอและการเยี่ยมบ้านเป็นข้อตกลงเบื้องต้นในการติดตามผู้ป่วยวัณ โรคปอดในพื้นที่จังหวัดนนทบุรี เจ้าหน้าที่ โรงพยาบาลส่งเสริมสุขภาพตำบล ได้สะท้อนผลการดำเนินงานว่า มี ความเข้าใจในการดูแลผู้ป่วยวัณโรคปอดมากขึ้น รู้สึกมีส่วนร่วมในการดูแลมากขึ้น อีกทั้งสามารถแก้ไขปัญหา ต่างๆ ระหว่างการรักษาร่วมกัน During these months, follow-up visits were conducted once a week every Monday, totaling six times. Subsequently, a brainstorming session was held during a meeting to monitor operations, which included collecting data from in-depth interviews during the operational follow-up meeting and making observations during home visits to patients together with staff from the sub-district health-promoting hospitals and village health volunteers. Additionally, at every medication appointment, the remaining pills were counted concurrently. Of the 32 patients, all took their medication daily and attended their doctor appointments as scheduled. Moreover, patients' health behaviors regarding medication adherence and infection prevention improved due to receiving correct guidance from the sub-district health-promoting hospital staff. Furthermore, 50 household contacts were advised to get chest X-rays for tuberculosis screening at the hospital under their respective healthcare entitlements; all results were normal. Patients also practiced correct infection control measures. There was also feedback on the implementation of the plan, which proved effective in solving the problems faced by pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province, resulting in patients receiving continuous care and medication. Environmental improvements were made in patients' homes to reduce the spread of infection, and confidential patient information was transferred promptly and correctly. The meeting concluded with an agreement to continue monitoring patients, both through video-observed therapy and home visits, as the initial strategy for following up pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province. Sub-district health-promoting hospital staff reflected that they gained a better understanding of caring for pulmonary TB patients, felt more involved in care, and helped solve various issues collaboratively during treatment, which increased patients' confidence and motivation to complete their treatment. This also enhanced patient care and highlighted its importance.

N = NTIP base for Faultless and Continue Data: Utilizing the National Tuberculosis Information Program (NTIP) as a platform for transmitting, coordinating, and following up patient information between clinic staff at hospitals and sub-district health-promoting hospital staff. Sub-district health-promoting hospital staff closely supervise patients’ medication intake at scheduled times every day until treatment completion.

3.1 Results of Knowledge Assessment Regarding Tuberculosis Care Guidelines among the Sample Group  
It was found that among the 50 participants, the majority were female (70.00%), aged between 30–35 years (60.00%), held a bachelor's degree (86.00%), and worked as government officials (90.00%). The average knowledge score regarding tuberculosis care guidelines before the training was 12.64 points (mean = 12.64, SD = 1.52), which is considered low (less than 16 points). After the training, the average score increased to 19.31 points (mean = 19.31, SD = 2.74), which is considered high (more than 16 points). This demonstrates that the post-training mean knowledge score regarding tuberculosis care guidelines was significantly higher than the pre-training score (P-value < .001), as shown in Table 1.

3.2 Results of Implementation Assessed by Brainstorming Meetings, Observation, and In-Depth Interviews  
It was found that each patient who received home visits from sub-district health-promoting hospital staff together with village health volunteers demonstrated improved health care, attended all scheduled appointments, and took medications on time as prescribed. The patients exhibited better adherence to proper infection prevention measures and made adjustments to their environment to maximize preventive efforts. A staff member from a sub-district health-promoting hospital stated, “Since I started providing care and giving information to the patients, they have listened, adapted, and taken better care of themselves than before.” Furthermore, there was consistent attendance at scheduled appointments and proper medication adherence. A tuberculosis clinic staff member from a hospital commented, “The patients have never missed an appointment, possibly because the health facility has constantly followed up with them. They are now almost finished with their treatment and have never missed a single appointment.” Additionally, patients have improved their proper infection prevention practices. 1 January – February 2023

Enabling pulmonary tuberculosis patients to receive proper treatment and continued community-based care improves their quality of life.

3.3 Evaluation of the treatment success rate among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province was carried out through monitoring by a sample group under the developed patient follow-up model in Nonthaburi Province. This involved pulmonary tuberculosis patients currently under treatment within the catchment areas of public health staff at various sub-district health-promoting hospitals—a total of 32 cases. Among these, it was found that the 32 pulmonary tuberculosis patients who were monitored by local public health officials participating in the project had the following treatment outcomes: 30 patients were successfully treated, accounting for 93.75%, while 2 patients were transferred out, representing 6.25%, as shown in Table 2.

Table 2: Treatment success rates among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi who were monitored by the sample group under the developed follow-up model in Nonthaburi Province (n = 32)

Treatment Outcome       Number     Percentage
Successfully treated         30             93.75
Transferred out                2               6.25

Discussion of results

Situation analysis revealed ongoing challenges among local public health officials, including a lack of understanding about tuberculosis, incorrect guidance given to tuberculosis patients regarding self-care during treatment, and inadequate advice on preventing the spread of tuberculosis. In addition, most individuals overseeing patient medication adherence were family members without knowledge about patient medication protocols. There was also insufficient coordination and continuity in patient follow-up by area staff, which resulted in patients not consistently taking their medications. Staff lacked knowledge and experience in tuberculosis patient care, and preventive practices to control transmission of tuberculosis were incorrect. Furthermore, there was a lack of knowledge regarding guidelines for tuberculosis prevention, control, and ongoing community-based patient care. Tuberculosis clinic staff also lacked communication and referral processes to hand over patients to the community, leading to discontinuity in area-based patient follow-up. The NTIP program for tuberculosis patient data management was being used only at the hospital level. These findings are consistent with the study by Chantana Chaodorn et al. (2012), which found that pulmonary tuberculosis patients did not practice appropriate treatment, prevention of disease transmission, or adherence to follow-up appointments. Most treatment supporters did not take their roles in supervising patients’ medication seriously. Staffing levels in tuberculosis clinics were inadequate, and there was ambiguity in data transfer and patient follow-up procedures. This is also in line with the findings of Awinon Buaprachum et al. (2016), which showed a lack of community participation in patient care.

Pulmonary tuberculosis in the community has persisted because pulmonary tuberculosis patients have limited knowledge and understanding about the disease, and issues exist with medication adherence. Caregivers for pulmonary tuberculosis patients lack sufficient knowledge about tuberculosis and do not fully understand their roles. Village health volunteers also have inadequate knowledge and lack confidence in caring for pulmonary tuberculosis patients and searching for new cases within the community. In addition, related staff responsible for caring for pulmonary tuberculosis patients lack continuous guidelines or activities for ongoing care. The development of a pulmonary tuberculosis patient follow-up model in Nonthaburi Province using the AIC technique has enabled tuberculosis clinic staff and sub-district health-promoting hospital staff to have a clear operational framework. This has promoted cooperation in planning, which is consistent with the study by Srisurang Duangpraserth (2020), who developed a care model for pulmonary tuberculosis patients with the participation of village health volunteers using a participatory AIC planning process to develop a care model in Nakhon Nayok Province. Furthermore, the development of this model can be applied to groups of public health staff to enable genuine participation in the creation of practical action plans and provide a clear framework. The developed model consists of: 1) aspects of care and treatment, 2) prevention of transmission and contact tracing, 3) promoting knowledge and self-care behaviors during treatment, 4) environmental management, 5) supervision and follow-up of medication intake, and 6) follow-up visits. The AIC technique helps to concretely encourage participation. This aligns with the study by Awinon Buaprachum et al. (2016), who developed a community-based pulmonary tuberculosis patient care model for sub-district health-promoting hospitals in Mueang District, Phitsanulok Province. ดังนั้นรูปแบบการติดตามผู้ป่วยวัณโรคปอดในพื้นที่จังหวัดนนทบุรี ทำให้อัตราความสำเร็จการรักษา เพิ่มขึ้นได้เป็นอย่างดี และรูปแบบนี้สามารถนำไปใช้ได้จริงทั้งจังหวัดนนทบุรี รวมถึงเจ้าหน้าที่ในพื้นที่ได้มีส่วน ร่วมในการดูแลผู้ป่วยวัณโรคทำให้การติดตามผู้ป่วยเป็นไปอย่างราบรื่น สามารถติดตามผู้ป่วยได้จริงและ สามารถทำได้อย่างต่อเนื่อง ทำให้ผู้ป่วยสามารถกินยาได้อย่างสม่ำเสมอ ส่งผลให้สามารถลดการแพร่กระจาย เชื้อในครอบครัวและชุมชน รวมถึงสามารถสร้างแนวทางที่ชัดเจนและเหมาะกับบริบทพื้นที่ของจังหวัดนนทบุรี มากที่สุดในการดูแลและติดตามผู้ป่วยวัณโรคปอด ซึ่งในอนาคต NON TB MODEL จะผลักดันให้เป็นแนวทาง ในการบริหารจัดการภายในจังหวัดเพื่อให้บรรลุเป้าหมายอัตราความสำเร็จการรักษาผู้ป่วยวัณโรคที่ร้อยละ 85 ตามแนวทางของสำนักวัณโรค กรมควบคุมโรค (2558) ที่ว่า “ค้นให้พบ จบด้วยหาย ไม่แพร่กระจาย”

Knowledge about disease and appropriate practices for pulmonary tuberculosis patients and their caregivers was assessed through home visit follow-ups. 3) The plan for continuous care of pulmonary tuberculosis patients within the community involved evaluating the sample group's knowledge of tuberculosis care guidelines. The mean score of knowledge regarding tuberculosis care guidelines after the training was significantly higher than before the training (P-value <.001). This is consistent with the study by Srisurang Duangprasert (2020), which found that the knowledge regarding tuberculosis patient care before and after training differed significantly at the 0.05 level. Moreover, the implementation of the pulmonary tuberculosis patient follow-up model in Nonthaburi Province enabled patients to receive proper treatment and continuous community care, consequently improving their quality of life. This aligns with the study by Anupan Prajam (2021), which found that the overall continuity of care behaviors for tuberculosis patients before and after development differed significantly, and that the action-based activities improved the quality of tuberculosis patient care. Family-centered nursing care is thus essential, engaging families in patient care, fostering close bonds, mutual assistance, and coordination with relevant agencies, which promotes successful treatment outcomes. Patients and their families develop mental strength, self-reliance, and a better quality of life.  
Furthermore, the evaluation of the treatment success rate for pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi, monitored by the sample group under the developed follow-up model, revealed a treatment success rate of 93.75%, meeting the national target of above 85% (Tuberculosis Division, Department of Disease Control, 2021). This is consistent with the study by Phakadao Promsuri (2020), which found that after using the Quality Wheel 3C Model, the treatment success rate for tuberculosis patients increased: in 2011, it was 96.7%, and from 2012–2018, it reached 100.0%.  
Therefore, the follow-up model for pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province can significantly increase the treatment success rate. This model is feasible for application throughout Nonthaburi Province, involving local staff in patient care and ensuring smooth, continuous follow-up so that patients can take medication regularly. This reduces transmission within families and communities while also establishing clear, context-appropriate guidelines for patient care and monitoring in Nonthaburi Province. In the future, the NON TB MODEL will be promoted as an internal provincial management guideline to achieve the treatment success rate target of 85% in accordance with the Tuberculosis Division, Department of Disease Control (2015) principle: “Find them, cure them, stop the spread.”

Summary and Recommendations

This study utilized participatory action research processes together with the participatory planning technique, AIC, resulting in successful implementation. The analysis produced findings on the situation regarding the care and follow-up of pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province, the development of a follow-up model for pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province based on the NON TB MODEL, and the evaluation of the use of the follow-up model among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nonthaburi Province. The results showed that staff knowledge concerning tuberculosis care guidelines significantly increased (P-value <.001), and the treatment success rate among patients in Nonthaburi Province who were followed up under the developed model reached 93.75%.

Recommendations: Provincial-level agencies should organize training to enhance staff capacity in tuberculosis care guidelines at least once a year. Community public health staff should emphasize patient follow-up to monitor for side effects of tuberculosis medications and provide accurate and appropriate advice to patients and their families. Community public health staff should directly supervise patient medication intake in all forms, whether in-person or via video, to ensure medication adherence throughout the treatment period. The care of pulmonary tuberculosis patients in the community should involve other agencies, such as local administrative organizations, to participate in effective tuberculosis prevention and control. In future studies, the model should be applied in other contexts, such as other provinces with similar urban settings.
